review_notes: I read the whole file and the definition of residueTestMean. I also read the one downstream use in BiasedPrimeBlock.lean and grepped the Ostmann directory for other uses. The file has no @[simp] attributes and no simp-set conflicts or loops. The only real issue is that biasedPrimeBand has no membership lemma. I did not run Lean, so I make no claim about how simp behaves. The weak point is that there are only two uses, so the gain is modest.

findings.excerpt:
noncomputable def biasedPrimeBand (A : Set ℕ) (N : ℕ) (T δ : ℝ) (t : ℕ → ℤ) : Finset ℕ :=
  (logPrimeBand T).filter fun p => δ ≤
findings.problem: biasedPrimeBand is a noncomputable def wrapping a Finset.filter, and the file provides no interface lemma for it. There is no membership characterisation, and no subset lemma for biasedPrimeBand ⊆ logPrimeBand T. Users have to reach through the definition. Inside this file, biasedPrimeBand_weight needs a `change _ ≤ ∑ p ∈ biasedPrimeBand ... at hh` to turn the `∑ p ∈ P.filter ...` from weighted_bias_threshold into the band. That `change` only works by definitional unfolding. The downstream file does the same with `Finset.mem_filter.mp hp` (for example `(Finset.mem_filter.mp hp).2`) and with `Finset.filter_subset _ _` against the unfolded body. A simp lemma for membership would let `simp` and `simp only` rewrite `p ∈ biasedPrimeBand A N T δ t` to its band-and-bias form, where today the definition has to be unfolded.
findings.proposed_change:
Add right after the definition:
`@[simp] theorem mem_biasedPrimeBand {A N T δ t p} : p ∈ biasedPrimeBand A N T δ t ↔ p ∈ logPrimeBand T ∧ δ ≤ |residueTestMean (tailSupport A N p) (quadraticResidueTest p (t p))| := Finset.mem_filter`
Also add `biasedPrimeBand_subset : biasedPrimeBand A N T δ t ⊆ logPrimeBand T := Finset.filter_subset _ _`. The `change` in biasedPrimeBand_weight could then become `rw [biasedPrimeBand]` or a `show`. In BiasedPrimeBlock, hQband and hQbias could use biasedPrimeBand_subset and `(mem_biasedPrimeBand.mp hp).2`.
findings.benefit: Membership in the band gets one canonical simp-normal form (`p ∈ logPrimeBand T ∧ δ ≤ |…|`). Downstream proofs no longer unfold the definition or use `change` and raw `Finset.mem_filter`, so they do not depend on the internal filter encoding.
